implementation_notes: When the service is a NestJS application the structure is provided by Terminus: TerminusModule contributes HealthCheckService and a set of indicators (HTTP, TypeORM, Mongoose, Sequelize, MikroORM, Prisma, microservice, gRPC, memory, disk), the controller exposes them with @Get() plus the @HealthCheck() decorator, per-indicator withTimeout(ms) bounds each check, and the report shape is fixed ({status: 'ok' | 'error' | 'degraded' | 'shutting_down', info, error, details}) - so the registry, aggregation and transport mapping collapse into decorators and indicator calls. Where the stack is Express or Fastify instead, the pattern is a plain handler and the type-level contribution becomes the contract: type the report (status union plus per-indicator details) once and reuse it in the probes' documentation and the tests.
idiom_name: @nestjs/terminus HealthCheckService with indicators, or a typed route handler
pitfalls: Indicators execute per request: a check without withTimeout can exceed the orchestrator's probe deadline, and the resulting connection reset is read as an unreachable instance instead of an unhealthy one.
The report distinguishes degraded from error, but a handler that maps every non-ok status to 503 turns a partial degradation into a full outage - decide the status-code mapping per endpoint.
Shutdown hooks change the reported status to shutting_down; with hooks disabled the readiness endpoint keeps answering ok while the process drains, so the decider keeps routing traffic to it.
